analysis: The only changed line in this PR is provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Startup/StartupPreloadTests.swift:885. The test stub NoEvictStubLanguageModel.prepare signature moves from (input, cache, windowSize) to (input, cache, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters), tracking an upstream LanguageModel protocol change in the MLX dependency. The change is test-only. It touches no production code, key handling, attestation, coordinator protocol, prefix-cache crypto or storage (T-041), authorization (TB-011/T-053), or trust boundaries. I read the rest of the file, which covers StartupPreloader admission, the startup gate and fail-closed self-test retirement. It is unchanged context and creates no new attack surface. Tests write temporary files under the temp directory and fake HF snapshots under ModelScanner.defaultCacheDirectory(), cleaned up with defer. This is the existing test pattern and not a production risk. Remaining unverified: the production LanguageModel protocol and dependency version bump, which are in other files not supplied here. The next pass should confirm that the dependency update does not change security-relevant semantics, such as prefill or state handling in cache salt scoping. Nothing in the supplied evidence indicates a regression.
